newsitem.title: INDIA: Israel firm ties up with India Nagarjuna.
newsitem.headline: Israel firm ties up with India Nagarjuna.

text.p: India's Nagarjuna Fertilizers and Chemicals Ltd said it was setting up a joint venture with Israel's Haifa Chemicals to make speciality fertilisers.

The joint venture would be 60 percent owned by Nagarjuna and 40 percent by the Israeli firm, P.R. Menon, Nagarjuna's director (technical) told a news conference to discuss the firm's financial results for the year ended March 31, 1997.

The cost of the new firm had not been firmed up, but should be around 40 to 50 million rupees, Menon said. He said Haifa Chemicals is the world's largest producer of potassium nitrate and other speciality fertilisers.
Nagarjuna Fertilzers and Chemicals has been successfully trial marketing the speciality fertilisers in Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Orissa during the past one year.
Nagarjuna is a leading urea producer in southern India.
